fields.summary: Autonomous plan run, no owner. Diagnosis: ship-change run 01M7786QKAZMH7PBJZP7QQA6HX failed at step land because change set 01M763YX47S5XY0W3P8FVJ54S8 (Rhiza's Go behaviour moves, PR 475) updated root-daemon-settings-scope's statement on a base that change set 01M763Z16T0ZGQMY1EC2Y81V0K (auto-update, PR 473) had since superseded with its own statement write. rhiza land refused it as a model conflict (exit 3). land's on.fail goes to land-triage, which runs rhiza ship gate --failed and passes only a recorded pre-push failure, so the run ended and the watchdog filed this bug. The orchestrator repaired it by hand with rhiza set --rebase, keeping both edits (commit 480b6acf3), and the land retry passed. The planner asked how ship-change should handle such a refusal: an agent repair step, an inbox question, or code auto-rebase. The arbiter decided ship-land-model-conflict-rebase: land-triage tells a model conflict apart from other failures and routes it to a model-conflict fixer agent that rebases each stale update with rhiza set --rebase so both edits hold, commits with Change: and Actor: trailers, and returns through gate-land to land. The fixer has a max_visits cap and asks one blocking question on a real clash. Every other land failure ends the run as now. The planner split the work into two leaves: ship land records the conflict for a triage check (internal/api), and the built-in workflow's routes and fixer step.
fields.title: Plan: ship-change recovers from a land refused for a model conflict (autonomous)
